description.p: A human studies the flow of battle, watching sparks fade against stone and steel trace its familiar arcs. With a deliberate stroke through the air, she fixes the moment in place, and flame follows the path she has chosen.
Crouched behind cover, a half-elf measures distance and motion before releasing a wash of numbing cold, reshaping the field long enough for his allies to press the attack.
An Artist stands within the chaos, tools in hand, applying force and color with intention. Each choice is deliberate. Each action builds toward a greater work.

Artists are spellcasters who treat the world as a canvas. Rather than relying on overwhelming spellcasting, they shape magic through discipline, precision, and commitment. By establishing a canvas in the world and working upon it step by step, an Artist creates effects that resolve the battle according to their vision.

Though their magic is narrower than that of other casters, Artists excel at controlling space and momentum. Their greatest works demand focus and patience, while practiced techniques keep them effective even as a larger composition takes form.
Whatever their origin, all Artists share the same belief: magic, like art, is strongest when guided by intent.

Artists are adventurers first and foremost. Their power does not come from vast reserves of magic, but from a practiced ability to respond to the moment before them. Through passion, discipline, and an eye for opportunity, they shape the world in small but meaningful ways, turning chaos into composition.

An Artist learns to read motion, terrain, and intent, applying force only where it matters. Whether reinforcing an ally’s advance, controlling a dangerous space, or building toward a decisive moment, they adapt their expression to the demands of the situation. Even when their magic is limited, their presence alters the flow of battle.

Though their works often require time and commitment, Artists are rarely idle. Through constant practice and experimentation, they remain effective in nearly any environment, finding ways to impose form even with limited tools. Where others rely on overwhelming strength or preparation, an Artist relies on awareness, restraint, and vision.

Artists are often regarded with a mixture of curiosity and unease. Their work is difficult to explain, their methods stranger still, and their willingness to place themselves in danger can appear reckless to outsiders. Many people see Artists as unstable—individuals who chase sensation and conflict rather than comfort or certainty.

In truth, an Artist could live a quieter life. Many are capable of earning coin through simple commissions, demonstrations, or small-scale work in settled lands. Yet few remain satisfied. The unpredictable nature of adventuring—its violence, motion, and constant change—provides a depth of experience that cannot be replicated in safety. For an Artist, chaos is not a hazard to be avoided, but a medium to be explored.

As adventurers, Artists are rarely driven by greed or duty alone. Some travel in search of inspiration, others to test the limits of their expression, and a few to leave behind works that will never be forgotten. Whatever their reason, Artists tend to thrive where the world is unstable, finding clarity and purpose in moments when everything else threatens to come apart.

When creating an Artist, consider the experiences and passions that shaped their approach to magic. What sights, moments, or emotions do they seek to capture through their work? Was there a single event that inspired them to pursue art above all else, or did their calling emerge gradually through experimentation and obsession?

Think about how your Artist learned their craft. Were they mentored by another Artist, trained in an informal collective, or entirely self-taught through trial, failure, and persistence? Many Artists follow no formal tradition, developing their expression through instinct and personal philosophy rather than structured study.

Artists are often driven by goals that lack clear resolution. They may chase inspiration, perfection, recognition, or understanding—pursuits that cannot be neatly completed. This uncertainty draws them toward the unpredictable life of an adventurer, where danger and chaos provide constant opportunity for growth.

Though their methods may appear unconventional, an Artist is far from dead weight in an adventuring party. Their adaptability, discipline, and ability to shape the flow of conflict make them valuable allies, especially when situations demand creativity rather than brute force.

You can create an Artist quickly by following these suggestions. First, make Wisdom your highest ability score, as it governs your perception, discipline, and control over your work. Your next highest score should be Dexterity if you favor mobility and positioning, or Constitution if you expect to maintain focus under pressure.

Second, choose the Artisan Guild, Entertainer, Hermit, or Sage background. Each reflects a different path into artistic practice, from formal training to solitary experimentation or public performance.
As an Artist, you gain the following class features.

ul.li: Hit Points at 1st Level: 6 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier per Artist level after 1st
Tools: Calligrapher’s supplies or painter’s supplies
Skills: Choose two from Arcana, History, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, and Religion

description.p: You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

ul.li: An infused brush, which functions as your spellcasting focus
(a) an explorer’s pack or (b) a scholar’s pack
